s22-tomato-nearest.intro: A tomato has sweetness 6 and crunchiness 4. We compare it with four labeled foods and give it the class of the one food it is most similar to, using the Euclidean distance.
s22-tomato-nearest.end: The tomato is a fruit because its single nearest food, orange at 1.41421, is a fruit. With only one neighbor, one odd food near the tomato would decide the class on its own.

s22-medicine-distance.intro: Medicine 1 has features (MW, pH) = (1, 1) and medicine 4 has (5, 4), both on arbitrary scales. We compare the Euclidean, Manhattan and Minkowski (p = 3) distances between them.
s22-medicine-distance.end: The same two medicines are 7, 5 or 4.49794 apart depending on the distance used. A larger p gives more weight to the biggest single difference, so the distance moves toward 4 as p grows.

s22-ages-kmeans.1: Every age gets a distance to both centroids, and the full table lists all ten rows.
s22-ages-kmeans.end: The algorithm stops at iteration 3 because no age changed cluster, so the centroids 22.75 and 40.83333 are final. The two groups are ages 20 to 28 and ages 35 to 44, which can be named young and old.

s22-medicines-kmeans.intro: Four medicines have features (MW, pH) on arbitrary scales of (1, 1), (2, 1), (4, 3) and (5, 4). Cluster them with k-means using k = 2, initial centroids c1 = (1, 1) and c2 = (2, 1), and the Euclidean distance.
s22-medicines-kmeans.end: Medicines 1 and 2 form one cluster and medicines 3 and 4 form the other. The centroids (1.5, 1) and (4.5, 3.5) are final because a third pass leaves every label the same.

s22-exercise-sbp-crp.intro: Systolic blood pressure (SBP) and C-reactive protein (CRP) were measured in 3 adults and standardized, so the values are unitless. Do one iteration of k-means with k = 2 and the Euclidean distance, starting from C1 = (2, 2) and C2 = (5, 5).
s22-exercise-sbp-crp.0: Patient 1 is (1, 3), so we find its distance to C1 and to C2.
s22-exercise-sbp-crp.1: Patient 2 is (7, 2), so we find its distance to C1 and to C2.
s22-exercise-sbp-crp.2: Patient 3 is (8, 7), so we find its distance to C1 and to C2.
s22-exercise-sbp-crp.end: Patient 1 is in cluster 1 and patients 2 and 3 are in cluster 2, so the new centroids are C1 = (1, 3) and C2 = (7.5, 4.5). This is one iteration only, so the labels would be checked again with these new centroids.

s22-ages-withinss.intro: The ages 20, 21, 22, 28 (centroid 22.75) and 35, 40, 41, 42, 43, 44 (centroid 40.83333) are the final clusters from kmeans(age, c(21, 30)) in R. Reproduce withinss, tot.withinss and betweenss, then use the R results for k = 3 and 4 to choose k.
s22-ages-withinss.4: The drop from k = 1 to k = 2 is about 785, and the later drops are only about 53 and 24.5.
s22-ages-withinss.end: Two clusters are chosen because going from one to two clusters removes about 785 of the 874.4 total, while a third or fourth cluster removes only about 53 and 24.5 more.

s22-tomato-knn.0: Rounded to one decimal these are 2.2, 4.2, 3.6 and 1.4.
s22-tomato-knn.end: The tomato is called a fruit because two of its three nearest neighbors, orange and grape, are fruits. The third neighbor, nuts, is a protein, so the probability of fruit is 2/3 and not 1.

s22-mesh-knn.intro: Mesh from four vendors was graded Pass or Fail by surgeons, with strength (x1, kg/m²) and flexibility (x2, integer scale 1 to 10) measured. A new vendor's mesh has x1 = 7 and x2 = 3. Classify it with K-NN using K = 3 and the Euclidean distance.
s22-mesh-knn.end: The new mesh is classified as Fail because two of its three nearest vendors, C and D, failed. Vendor A passed, so the probability of failing is 2/3. This call needs no expensive review by surgeons.
